classification.difficultyReason: Choose the exposed two curved walls, top disk and annulus, excluding the table contact and hidden contact disks.

content.prompt: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm is mounted on a cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 5 cm. Find the area of the visible surfaces, if the larger cylinder is sitting on a table. Give an exact answer and an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Explicit source coaxial cylinders outerr6/h5 andupperr3/h4. Draw lower cylinder first; actual opaque upper cylinder silhouette hides lower top far rim that passes behind its body. Exposed contact near arc solid, concealed contact far arc reference dashed. Uppertop fullrim, outerbottomnear/far correct. White is actual upper material side face, never annotation/background trick. Independent source-hashed curved visibility review required. No numerical dimensions added to given figure.
spec.answerVisibility: Original source givens only; no derived answer labels.

answer.worked:
Exclude the lower bottom on the table and the contact disks between the cylinders. Add the two curved walls, upper top and exposed lower top annulus.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2\pi(6)(5)+2\pi(3)(4)+\pi(3)^2+\pi(6^2-3^2)\\S&=(60+24+9+27)\pi=120\pi\text{ cm}^2\\S&\approx377.00\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
